selected_problem: A truth-boundary evidence revision can currently suppress its own boundary row by listing that same source/path in `resolves`, because the bridge applies a file's resolution references before evaluating the file's own boundary rows. That lets a single revision erase its own unresolved evidence without any newer closure provenance and can make diagnosis falsely report NO_ACTIONABLE_CANDIDATE.

execution.route_basis: Fresh main exposes a single narrow, directly reproducible provenance defect in the truth-boundary ledger. The candidate is highly central to autonomous diagnosis, has dense local evidence, and does not require a product-shape or architecture decision, so source-contract replay routes this cycle to DEEP_DEVELOPMENT without forced mode rotation.

changes: Resolution references from the current evidence file are now added only after that file's own boundary rows have been evaluated.
Only resolution provenance already observed in newer revisions may suppress the current older revision's rows.
Newer evidence still resolves explicitly referenced older source/path rows exactly as before; no semantic closure inference or hard-coded roadmap is introduced.

validation.pre_fix_reproduction: REPRODUCED: an evidence file containing `resolves: [{source: 'evidence/self.json', path: 'truth_boundaries[0]'}]` plus `truth_boundaries: ['UNRESOLVED: same revision must stay visible']` caused the unpatched bridge to emit RuntimeError: NO_ACTIONABLE_CANDIDATE instead of exposing the boundary.

truth_boundaries: Explicit source/path resolution remains committed provenance, not semantic proof that arbitrary uncited historical boundaries are closed.
This closes same-revision self-suppression only; it does not claim cryptographic authenticity for evidence files or protect against a malicious writer with repository write access.
BLOCKED_EXTERNAL: GitHub's merge REST endpoint still lacks an atomic expected-base-SHA precondition, so external GET-to-PUT base races remain outside client-side elimination.
